prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The document proposes Scottish independence and sets out policies across governance, economy, public services, environment, international relations, and a four‑year budget.

Constitution and route to independence
- Seek a majority mandate, negotiate terms with the UK and EU, then hold a referendum on the settlement before declaring independence and holding new elections.
- Establish a written constitution and Bill of Rights guaranteeing civil, social, and economic rights (including housing, education, healthcare, fair work).
- Create a single‑chamber parliament elected by proportional representation; extend voting to 16+; enable citizen petitions; reform ceremonial roles; entrench and elect local government by PR.
- Citizenship based on residency or birth; EU continuity of pensions and investments; open border with the rest of the UK.

Economy, jobs, and taxation
- Aim for full employment; target 100,000 additional jobs; national apprenticeships; export unit; skills foundation; double tourism marketing.
- Business taxation over four years: cut corporation tax from 33p to 30p; small companies’ rate from 23p to 18p; abolish Class IV NICs; banded business rates with small‑firm focus; cap rate‑multiplier growth to RPI; merger/takeover and late‑payment reforms.
- Adopt EU Social Chapter; introduce a minimum wage at half median male earnings after consultation.
- Personal taxation: introduce a 15p starter income tax rate; widen the basic‑rate band by 15%; remove the National Insurance ceiling; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; raise tobacco duty; reduce spirits duty.

Health, social justice, and justice system
- Additional £35m per year for the NHS; abolish the internal market; reintegrate dentistry; review prescription charges; ban tobacco advertising; strengthen prevention and audit.
- Increase child benefit to £12.50; restore benefits for 16–17 year‑olds; raise state pensions by £3 (single) and £5 (couple) weekly; introduce a cold‑climate allowance; remove utility standing charges for pensioners; abolish means testing for residential elderly care; disability rights charter.
- Create an independent food and consumer health agency.
- Support community policing and crime reduction; vehicle‑history register; expand alternatives to prison; ban handguns and implement the Cullen recommendations.

Education, housing, local services, culture
- Hire 700 teachers; repair schools; internet access in every school; free nursery places for 3–4 year‑olds; restore student maintenance grants (1990 real terms); expand training subsidies; support Gaelic‑medium education and provision for other communities.
- Transfer 75% of council housing debt to central government over four years, enabling up to 20,000 affordable homes, major upgrades of substandard and damp homes; protect new/improved stock from discounted right‑to‑buy; create a new housing agency; strengthen homelessness duties.
- Restore more powers to local government; abolish water quangos; reform local finance (consider local income tax in a later term).
- Establish a Scottish public‑service broadcaster funded by the licence fee; film tax incentives; a unified “Scottish Screen”; equal status for Gaelic and Scots; a national lottery with smaller jackpots and no scratch cards.

Land, rural, environment, energy, transport, telecoms
- Abolish feudal tenure; create a Land Commission and open land register; transfer seabed/shore powers to councils.
- Agriculture: traceability, CAP reform, rural diversification fund (£10m/yr), improve market access.
- Forestry: National Forest Enterprise Board; double woodland cover in 25 years; boost wood‑using industries.
- Crofting: transform the Crofters Commission into a development agency; support community ownership.
- Fisheries: regional management councils; processing support; stronger enforcement; conservation measures; +£10m/yr for structural support, marketing, infrastructure, and research.
- Strengthen and make SEPA independent; set national environmental targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay; create a renewables R&D centre.
- Energy: allocate North Sea resources by equidistance; honour existing obligations; address gas network access; phase out nuclear generation while expanding renewables and conservation; review deep coal mining; tighter opencast controls.
- Transport: bring Scottish Railtrack assets into public ownership; electrify key lines; integrate and regulate buses; end bridge tolls (Skye first via shadow tolls then public ownership); support ferries; abolish APD in the Highlands and Islands and adjust elsewhere by fare; expand international links.
- Telecoms: stronger regulation and rural rollout; promote internet access for schools, homes, and business; support UHI distance learning; update cyber law.

Europe, defence, and international aid
- Full EU membership with voting rights, own commissioner, EU presidency in turn; proportional elections to the European Parliament; target CFP/CAP reforms and EU funds.
- Targeted diplomatic network; membership in the Commonwealth, Council of Europe, and UN; propose a British‑Isles association.
- Non‑nuclear defence forces (army ~9k regulars; navy ~5k; air ~6k, with reserves); withdraw Trident; phased NATO withdrawal while cooperating via other frameworks; establish a peacekeeping college; defence diversification and local procurement where lawful.
- Increase overseas aid to 0.7% of GDP within six years.

Budget framework (first four years)
- Fund measures via a claimed fiscal surplus relative to the UK, growth effects, defence and interest savings; dedicated business‑tax reduction fund; net balances used to repay £6.6bn of inherited national debt.
